questions: Should the three or more identical elements be consecutive (i.e., appear in a row) or can they be non‑consecutive positions in the sequence?
Is the output case‑sensitive, i.e., must we print exactly "Yes" and "No" with capital Y/N and lowercase rest?
If N is less than 3, what should the program output, or is such input guaranteed not to occur?
Are there any extra whitespace or newline requirements for the output (e.g., trailing newline after the word)?
Must the program handle multiple test cases in a single input file, or is there exactly one test case per file?
Are the values of A_i guaranteed to be within the given range, or should the solution validate them?
If the sequence contains more than three identical elements consecutively, does that still count as a valid "place"?
Should the program stop processing as soon as it finds any qualifying place, or must it examine the entire sequence before deciding?
answers: It means the same element must appear three or more times consecutively (e.g., 5 5 5), and you should only check consecutive triples where 1 \le i \le N-2.

It means the same element must appear three or more times consecutively (e.g., 5 5 5), and you should only check consecutive triples where 1 \le i \le N-2. Input The input is given from Standard Input in the following format: N A_1 A_2 \ldots A_N Output If there is a place in A where the same element appears three or more times in a row, print Yes. Otherwise, print No. Constraints - 3 \le N \le 100 - 1 \le A_i \le 100 - All input values are integers.
